title: PublicHealth AirPollutionClinicPanel

stats.done_summary: Successfully completed the PublicHealth AirPollutionClinicPanel research task. Conducted comprehensive analysis of daily panel data linking PM2.5 to respiratory healthcare utilization. Generated 13 figures, 4 analysis scripts, 2 output files, and a detailed 12,868-word research report with methodology, results, discussion, and policy implications. Key findings: PM2.5 shows significant association with respiratory visits (cumulative effect of 1.49 visits per µg/m³ over 7 days), with flu index being the strongest predictor. Policy implications include early warning systems and healthcare resource planning during pollution events.
